bead.title: claude-tui/step5: pooled session lifetime with /clear between turns + orphan reaper
bead.description:
Per ADR-013 design constraints #4 (session pool), #5 (empirical /clear semantics gate), #6 (orphan reaper).

WORK:
- Package-scope singleton pool, keyed by (harness, workdir). Depth 1 per key default; expandable for service-mode concurrency.
- Between turns: /clear command resets conversation; verify model selection persists and permission mode persists per the empirical gate.
- Orphan reaper: startup helper analogous to service_stale_harness_reaper.go that kills claude processes whose parent fiz PID is gone before constructing the pool. No persistent state.

GATE: ADR-013 constraint #5 requires verifying /clear semantics against the installed Claude CLI (resets history; doesn't reset model/permissions/auth). If /clear is unstable, fall back to per-Execute sessions (claude-p model) and document the cost.
bead.acceptance:
1) An empirical /clear semantics report exists under docs/helix/02-design/ documenting the verification: history reset, model persists, permission mode persists, auth persists, new transcript file path emitted via the next Stop hook. claude --version included.
2) If /clear semantics hold: pooled-session implementation with depth-1 default, package-scope singleton, per-(harness, workdir) key. Pool placement asserted by a test that confirms two distinct &claudetui.Runner{} instances share the pool.
3) If /clear is unstable on any of the verified dimensions: per-Execute sessions with cold-start cost documented; both branches pass the conformance suite.
4) Pool concurrent-claim safety: two simultaneous Execute calls on the same (harness, workdir) serialize on the pooled session (no race; no broken state); tested by a goroutine race test.
5) Pool eviction on /clear failure: if /clear emits an error or the session becomes unresponsive mid-turn, the pool evicts the session and the next Execute on that key gets a fresh session; tested with a synthetic /clear-failing fixture.
6) Orphan reaper integrated into runner startup; reaps claude processes whose parent fiz PID is gone. Reaper kill-and-recover test: spawn a session, fake-crash fiz (test helper kills the parent PID indirectly), restart, verify the new runner reaps the orphan before claiming the pool.
7) A focused integration test asserts second Execute on the same (harness, workdir) reuses the pooled session when /clear is supported (assertion: same PID, second call latency < first call latency by the expected Ink+auth startup margin).
8) Service-mode concurrency: pool depth >1 supported via configuration; a test exercises depth=3 with three concurrent Execute calls and asserts all three complete with three distinct pool slots.
9) go test ./internal/harnesses/claude-tui/... -count=1 green.
